queries.query: Survey and empirical studies of LLMs (GPT-family, Llama, Claude, etc.) applied to network operations (NetOps), including configuration generation, intent-to-configuration translation, and troubleshooting assistants
queries.rationale: Establish the state of applied work using foundation models for concrete NetOps tasks and identify common observed failure modes and evaluation practices.

queries.query: LLM-generated network configuration correctness: studies comparing generated configs against formal/specification-based validators (e.g., Batfish, NetKAT, VeriFlow) and rule-based validators
queries.rationale: Target literature that pairs generative outputs with deterministic/network-verification tools to measure correctness and safety.

queries.query: Failure modes and empirical phenomena in LLM-assisted operational workflows: hallucination, omission, incorrect assumptions about topology/state, invalid CLI syntax, unsafe changes, and out-of-distribution behavior
queries.rationale: Collect documented empirical phenomena and taxonomy of error types relevant to operational risk in NetOps.

queries.query: Mechanisms underlying LLM errors in structured generation tasks: exposure bias, tokenization/context truncation, chain-of-thought, tool-use failures, and training data distribution gaps
queries.rationale: Understand model-internal and training-data mechanisms that plausibly cause the operational failure modes observed in NetOps settings.

queries.query: Generate–validate–repair architectures and constrained generation methods for safe configuration synthesis (prompt engineering, constrained decoding, templates, constrained DSLs, post-hoc repair loops)
queries.rationale: Survey mitigation approaches that wrap LLM generation with validators/repairers or constrain models to reduce unsafe outputs.

queries.query: Tool-augmented LLM agents and orchestration frameworks (Toolformer, ReAct, LangChain) adapted for operational tasks and their impact on reliability
queries.rationale: Identify agentic frameworks and how tool calls (validators, simulators) change error profiles and reproducibility in NetOps tasks.

queries.query: Benchmarks and datasets for evaluating LLMs on networking tasks (NetOps benchmarks, AIOps datasets, configuration corpora) and critiques on their ecological/operational validity
queries.rationale: Locate existing benchmark suites and critical analyses of whether they reflect realistic operational risk and correctness requirements.

queries.query: Formal and deterministic network verification tools and semantics (NetKAT, VeriFlow, Batfish, header space analysis) and their use as ground-truth validators in experiments
queries.rationale: Compile authoritative sources on verification methods that can provide objective correctness metrics for generated configurations/rules.

queries.query: Evaluation methodologies for operational correctness: metrics (reachability, policy compliance, loop/failure injection tests), paired experimental designs, and uncertainty quantification in NetOps experiments
queries.rationale: Gather best-practice measurement approaches and statistical methods suitable for comparing mitigations and quantifying reliability.

queries.query: Simulated and emulated evaluation environments used in NetOps research (Mininet, ns-3, containerized topologies, network testbeds) and their suitability for LLM-driven change execution testing
queries.rationale: Identify evaluation platforms that can safely execute generated configurations and simulate operational impacts for reproducible experiments.

queries.query: Adversarial and distribution-shift analyses for LLMs in operational tasks: prompt adversaries, malicious inputs, and robustness evaluation methods
queries.rationale: Survey how adversarial conditions and OOD shifts affect model safety in NetOps and methods to test robustness.
source_preferences: security conference proceedings (USENIX Security, IEEE S&P)

queries.query: Human-in-the-loop, approval gating, and operator-AI interaction studies in NetOps: how human oversight changes outcome reliability and workflow integration
queries.rationale: Locate empirical and design work on combining human operators with automated suggestions to reduce risk and improve trust.

queries.query: Related fields: program synthesis for config generation, automated patch/repair in software engineering, and lessons from AIOps and infrastructure-as-code safety research
queries.rationale: Draw transferable methods, metrics, and failure-analyses from adjacent domains that address structured generation, verification, and repair.

queries.query: Ethical, regulatory, and safety frameworks relevant to autonomous NetOps agents and operator accountability
queries.rationale: Identify ethical/safety guidance and regulatory considerations to frame mitigations, disclosure, and deployment claims.
source_preferences: policy whitepapers (OECD, EU AI Act analyses)

inclusion_criteria: Primary sources (peer-reviewed papers, arXiv preprints, tool project documentation) that present empirical results, methods, or formal analyses relevant to LLMs/Generative AI applied to network operations or to verification/mitigation methods.
Benchmarks, datasets, and reproducible artifacts (code repositories, datasets) with sufficient metadata to permit reuse or replication.
Work covering deterministic network verification tools, network simulators/emulators, and operator-in-the-loop studies relevant to correctness/trustworthiness.
Methodological and survey papers that synthesize failure modes, mitigation approaches, or evaluation methodologies applicable to NetOps.
exclusion_criteria: Pure marketing materials or vendor promotional blog posts without technical details or reproducible evidence.
Non-English sources unless primary technical content is otherwise unavailable (note and justify inclusion when used).
Opinion pieces or short editorials without references or empirical/methodological substance.
Proprietary/closed datasets or internal incident reports that cannot be cited or independently verified.
date_rationale: Include foundational network-verification and configuration literature irrespective of age (e.g., NetKAT, Batfish origins) while prioritizing work from 2018–2026 for LLM and AIOps developments (LLM rapid advances since ~2020). Aim to capture the most recent preprints and technical reports through 2026 to ensure currency for CNSM 2026 positioning.
